output.brief: The Android drop is almost certainly caused by a new Corvane edge rule, not by release 6.14. The 3 March rule-pack update added a rule (AUTO-LIB-17) that blocks password requests carrying the nettle-http user-agent. That is the library every Android version uses. Blocking began at 10:41 UTC on 3 March, about three minutes after the rule pack activated. The same drop appears on every app version, including 6.11 and older, and on every OS version, whether or not the March security patch is installed. Quick-unlock, iOS and web are unaffected. Password success fell from 96% to 8%. About 41,300 install IDs were blocked, and 92% of them had logged in successfully in the previous 90 days, so these are real customers and not bots. So a rollback of 6.14 would not help. Raising bot sensitivity would block more customers. Dropping blocked attempts from the KPI would hide the problem. Next step: ask Corvane today to set the rules added in 2026.03.1 to log-only on the mobile password-login path. Keep rate limits, lockout and all other rules active. Then confirm in telemetry that password success returns to about 96%. Continue the 6.14 rollout while you do. I'm fairly confident, around 90%.
